chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): What is for the man from his wealth at the time of his death? He said, 'One-third and one-third is a lot.'

key_terms.عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: at the time of his death

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum portion of wealth one can bequeath in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the upper limit of bequest (wasiyyah) by stating that 'one-third and one-third' (i.e., two-thirds) is excessive, thereby establishing the preferred maximum at one-third to preserve the heirs' rights. This ruling aligns with the general Islamic principle that a will should not encroach significantly on the fixed shares of inheritance, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a precautionary measure to ensure family stability. The phrasing highlights the distinction between the permissible maximum and the recommended limit, reflecting the Imam's emphasis on moderation in financial dispositions.
